questions.q: What does a firewall do at a network boundary?
options: Translates domain names to IP addresses
Inspects traffic against a rule set and allows or blocks it
Encrypts traffic between two servers
Balances traffic across multiple servers
questions.explain: A firewall sits at a boundary and inspects traffic against rules, allowing or blocking it; it doesn't encrypt, translate names, or balance traffic.

questions.q: What does stateful filtering let a firewall do?
options: Block all traffic regardless of rules
Automatically allow return traffic for a connection it already allowed outbound
Translate private IP addresses to public ones
Cache DNS answers for faster lookups
questions.explain: Stateful firewalls track existing connections and automatically permit the matching return traffic, without needing a separate rule for each direction.

questions.q: How does a cloud security group differ from a traditional network firewall?
options: It can only block outbound traffic
It's scoped to one resource or instance rather than an entire network segment
It requires a dedicated physical appliance
It only works with UDP traffic
questions.explain: A security group is a virtual firewall attached directly to one instance, unlike a traditional firewall protecting a whole network segment.

questions.q: In a firewall rule, what does the "source" field specify?
options: The protocol being used
Where the traffic is allowed to originate from
The destination port number
Whether the rule is stateful or stateless
questions.explain: The source field defines which address or range the rule applies to as the origin of the traffic.

Blocking everything by default and opening only what's explicitly needed
Denying only traffic on port 443
A setting that only applies to outbound traffic
questions.explain: Default deny blocks all traffic unless a rule explicitly permits it, which is the safest starting posture for any firewall or security group.
